title: Harissa Shakshuka with Feta
cuisine_note: Shakshuka travels from the Maghreb to the Levant; this version leans on harissa for depth instead of a long-cooked pepper base, which is what makes it weeknight-feasible.

qty.note: red or green; softening peppers past their prime is exactly what this sauce wants - the use-it-up tag is for them

steps.text: Warm the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper with a pinch of the salt for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is translucent and the pepper has slumped.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute - pull it off the heat if it darkens past pale gold.
Stir in the harissa, cumin, and smoked paprika and fry for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens a shade and smells dusty-sweet rather than raw.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes with the remaining salt and the black pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens enough to hold a spoon-track.
Taste the sauce: it should taste sharply of tomato with a chili burn that arrives late. Add another spoonful of harissa here if you cook for heat-lovers.
Make a well with the spatula for each egg and crack an egg into it. Season the whites with a little salt and keep the yolks whole.

Cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still move when the pan is jostled. Eggs are safe at 160°F (71°C); open one well and spot-check the thickest white with a thermometer.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Scatter the feta and parsley over the pan and carry it to the table as is - the feta softens from the steam rather than melting.
Serve straight from the skillet with rice or a green salad to round the meal.
